summary:
### Key Topics Discussed
- Discussed three open questions: the nature of the rules, the level at which the rule is set, and how dependent articles are categorized.
- The possibility of setting rules at article, order concept, or object level.
- Clarification on how dependent jobs should behave when the main job is moved.
- The concept of "frozen" versus "soft" offset for scheduling.

### Decisions Made
- The rule for dependent articles will be set at the company settings level under a "Dependent Articles" heading.
- Dependent articles will have a tolerance of plus or minus one hour.
- Dependent articles will be scheduled within a time window of 8 AM to 4 PM.
- The decision was made to initially set the rule at the company level. Future adjustments to article, order concept, or object level can be made if needed.
- For dependent jobs where the main job is moved, the dependent job (the "tail") will move with the main job in the performer's plan.
- Offsets for dependent jobs cannot be absolute; they must include a time window (e.g., three hours plus/minus one hour) to avoid constant rescheduling.

### Important Points & Insights
- The most logical approach for setting rules for dependent articles seems to be at the company level, or to integrate it when defining a dependent article to another article. The decision on the exact model for implementation will be based on what is easiest to code.
- Maintaining delivery times will be challenging without a flag indicating upcoming changes.

### Open Questions/Pending Items
- The exact nature of "reglernas natur" (the rules' nature) was initially an open question, which is now addressed by the decision to set the rule at the company settings level, with the flexibility for future adjustments.
- The question of "frozen" versus "soft" offset remains open/parked.
